verdict.rationale: WorkOS AuthKit documents a first-party CLI Auth feature built on the OAuth 2.0 Device Authorization Flow (RFC 8628). A device authorization endpoint issues a device code and user code, and the client then polls for tokens, so command-line apps authenticate through the web instead of using stored secrets. missing for 10: explicit documentation of headless/AI-agent use beyond CLIs, independent or hands-on corroboration of the device flow.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can authenticate CLIs and headless agents via the OAuth device authorization flow instead of pasting long-lived secrets

citations.quote: CLI Auth enables command-line applications to authenticate users through the web using the OAuth 2.0 Device Authorization Flow
a device authorization URL obtains a device code and user code, then tokens are polled for the session.
OAuth applications are designed for applications where the actor being authenticated is a User. These include web applications, mobile, desktop, and CLI tools.
